hook.line: Vale is putting signs up in the café kitchen, mostly to protect her cakes from Tomás. Signs, recipes and forms in Spanish talk to nobody in particular, so they use the plain dictionary form of the verb.

examples.es: No dejar comida en la nevera.
examples.en: Do not leave food in the fridge.

rule:
On signs, in recipes and on forms, Spanish uses the plain verb, the *-ar*, *-er*, *-ir* form from the dictionary. *No* goes in front.

English uses a command (Keep, Peel, Dial) or an *-ing* (No smoking). Spanish does neither: *No fumar*, *Mantener la puerta cerrada*.

It isn't rude. It speaks to anyone who reads it, so it never has to choose between *tú* and *usted*.

When you're talking to a real person, switch back to a command: *No fumes*, *Paga en la caja*.

options: Pay at the till. (to a friend)

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *fumar* or *fumes* and type the sign: *No ___.*
yourTurn.why: A sign talks to anyone, so the plain verb: *fumar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *Marca* or *Marcar* and type the printed instruction: *___ el número.*
yourTurn.why: Printed instructions use the dictionary form.

yourTurn.prompt: Write a sign for the kitchen: Do not touch the cakes.
yourTurn.why: *No* in front, then the plain verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Write the first step of a recipe: Peel and chop the onion.
yourTurn.why: Both verbs stay in the plain form, joined by *y*.

yourTurn.prompt: Write a sign for the door: Keep the door closed.
You're talking to a friend now, not writing a sign: *No fumar.*
yourTurn.why: Speaking to a friend, you switch to the *tú* command: *No fumes*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn what you'd say to a friend into a sign: *Paga en la caja.*
yourTurn.why: A sign uses the plain verb: *pagar*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. English says No smoking, but Spanish uses the plain verb: *fumar*.
On a sign for everyone, use the plain verb; *No fumes* is said to one friend.
*No* goes in front of the verb, never after it.

personal: Write two signs for your own kitchen or front door, with *No* plus a plain verb and one plain verb on its own (*No dejar...*, *Cerrar...*).
